notice: RN bank batch 133: Mental health case studies: Alzheimer sundowning, alcohol use disorder with Wernicke encephalopathy, ECT and complicated grief. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that could be driving the afternoon agitation.

rationale.correct: Pain, constipation, poor sleep and relocation can trigger sundowning.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of triggers for agitation in dementia.

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it fits dementia or delirium.

rows.text: Gradual decline over years
Sudden onset over hours to days
Attention fluctuates through the day
Usually reversible when the cause is treated
Alert, with memory loss

rationale.correct: Onset, course and attention separate the two; delirium can sit on top of dementia.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should first {{b1}}, because antipsychotics in older adults with dementia {{b2}}.

options.text: look for and treat causes such as pain, constipation and infection
give the haloperidol at 1600 every day
apply a belt restraint to the chair
move the client to a busier room
carry a boxed warning for increased death and stroke
are the first-line treatment
improve memory
have no side effects

rationale.correct: Find causes first; antipsychotics raise mortality in dementia.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include in the plan? Select all that apply.

options.text: Scheduled acetaminophen for knee pain
A bowel regimen
A calm, well-lit room in the late afternoon
A walking route and a meaningful activity at 1530
Reorient firmly that the children are grown
Daytime naps of 3 hours

rationale.correct: Treat pain and constipation, adjust the environment and plan activity.

perOption.e: Arguing with the reality increases distress.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Haloperidol order discontinued after team review.

questions.stem: At 1600, the client stands at the exit saying, "I have to get the children from school." Which responses are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Tell me about your children."
"Let's walk together and get a snack first."
Approach from the front at eye level, speaking slowly
"Your children are adults now; you're confused."
Block the door and hold the client's arms

rationale.correct: Validate the feeling and redirect.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest Wernicke encephalopathy.

rationale.correct: Confusion, eye signs and ataxia after glucose without thiamine is Wernicke encephalopathy.

perOption.r5: Low; withdrawal is not the cause.

questions.stem: For each statement by the client, indicate the defense mechanism.

rows.text: "I don't have a problem."
"I drink because my job is stressful."
"My wife is the one who drinks too much."
"I only drink what everyone else drinks."
"The lab test is wrong."

rationale.correct: Denial and rationalization are common in alcohol use disorder.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should {{b1}}, because untreated Wernicke encephalopathy can progress to {{b2}}.

options.text: give IV thiamine now as prescribed and before more glucose
increase the dextrose rate
give lorazepam
wait for an MRI
Korsakoff syndrome with permanent memory loss and confabulation
hepatic encephalopathy
delirium tremens
alcohol poisoning

rationale.correct: Thiamine before glucose prevents Korsakoff syndrome.

exhibits.title: Day 5
exhibits.body: Confusion improving on thiamine. Lipase falling. Client agrees to talk about drinking.

questions.stem: The client says, "Maybe I drink a bit too much." Which responses use motivational interviewing? Select all that apply.

options.text: "What worries you most about your drinking?"
"From 0 to 10, how ready are you?"
"Part of you wants to change."
"You're an alcoholic, and the first step is that you need to admit it."
"If you keep drinking like this, your pancreas will fail and you will die."

rationale.correct: Open questions, readiness and reflecting ambivalence.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll take thiamine every day."
"I'll go to my first AA meeting on Thursday."
"On naltrexone, I can't take my old oxycodone for my back."
"I'll start disulfiram tonight after my last beer."
"I'll avoid cough syrups and mouthwash with alcohol if I take disulfiram."

rationale.correct: Thiamine, support groups and correct medicine use.

perOption.r4:c2: Needs at least 12 hours without alcohol.

content.template: Because the client lacks capacity, consent for ECT comes from {{b1}}, and before the first session the nurse must {{b2}}.

options.text: a legally authorized representative or court, as state law requires
the nurse
any family member who visits
no one; it is an emergency
confirm signed consent and NPO status
give a large breakfast
give the evening lorazepam dose as usual
remove the ID band

Empty the bladder before the procedure

Expect ECT once only

Check vital signs and oxygen saturation
Reorient calmly and often
Raise side rails and supervise the first walk
Offer breakfast while still drowsy

options.text: immediate safety
grief counseling next month
a sleep aid
a dietitian referral
a same-day crisis evaluation and removing the rifle from the home
telling him time heals
asking him to promise not to hurt himself

options.text: Complicated grief therapy or a bereavement group

Daughter stores the rifle at her home
Senior center activities and a weekly check-in call
Advise him to clear out all her belongings this week
A nightly drink to help sleep

options.text: "Grief has no timetable. Tell me about her."
"You feel pressured and alone."

"You need to move on for your daughter's sake."
"I know exactly how you feel; I lost my own father last year."

exhibits.title: Long-term care admission
exhibits.body: A 79-year-old client with moderate Alzheimer disease moved into memory care yesterday. Each afternoon around 1600 the client becomes restless, tries to leave to "pick up the children from school" and pushes staff away. The client takes donepezil 10 mg at night. A new order reads haloperidol 2 mg IM as needed for agitation.

rows.label: Pain
cells: Grimaces when standing; history of knee arthritis

caseStudies.title: Alcohol use disorder with Wernicke encephalopathy

exhibits.title: Medical unit
exhibits.body: A 52-year-old client is admitted with pancreatitis. The client drinks a liter of vodka daily, eats little and says, "I don't have a problem. I can stop any time; my job just stresses me out." On day 2, an IV dextrose infusion is started for vomiting.

rows.label: Eyes
cells: Nystagmus; cannot move the eyes fully to the side

exhibits.title: Mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 67-year-old client with severe major depression with catatonia has stopped eating and drinking for 4 days, lies mute and rigid, and holds odd postures. Two antidepressant trials failed. Lorazepam IV gave only brief improvement. ECT is recommended.

caseStudies.title: Complicated grief in an older widower

exhibits.title: Clinic visit
exhibits.body: An 81-year-old client's wife of 55 years died 14 months ago. The client still sets her place at the table, has stopped seeing friends and says, "There's no point going on without her." The client lives alone, drinks whiskey each night and keeps a hunting rifle.

rows.label: Columbia scale
cells: Wish to be dead; thinking about how

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
